## 1. Public entry point: CloudFront

Operators visit an AWS-generated address such as:

https://d123example.cloudfront.net

CloudFront provides:

- A browser-trusted HTTPS certificate.
- The only public application entry point.
- The stable callback URL required by Cognito and Google OAuth.
- A private connection to the internal load balancer through a VPC origin.

Caching is disabled because this is an authenticated, dynamic application. Requests, cookies, query parameters, and WebSocket traffic are forwarded to Streamlit.

There is no custom domain or ACM certificate in this learning deployment.

## 2. Private entry layer: internal ALB

CloudFront forwards requests to an internal Application Load Balancer.

The ALB:

- Has no public endpoint.
- Lives in two private origin subnets across two Availability Zones.
- Accepts port 80 only from AWS’s CloudFront origin-facing network.
- Checks Streamlit’s /_stcore/health endpoint.
- Forwards healthy traffic to Streamlit on port 8501.

Using two subnets allows AWS to place the load balancer across two AZs. This makes the entry layer more resilient, although the application itself still has only one running task.

## 3. Application runtime: one Fargate task

ECS manages one Fargate task containing both application processes:

- Streamlit UI on port 8501.
- FastAPI on port 8000.

They are two containers built from the same immutable image digest.

Because containers in the same Fargate task share the task’s network interface, Streamlit calls FastAPI using:

http://127.0.0.1:8000

FastAPI is therefore not exposed through the ALB or CloudFront. Only Streamlit receives external application traffic.

The task is configured with:

- 0.5 vCPU.
- 1 GiB memory.
- An API health check.
- Streamlit startup only after the API becomes healthy.
- CloudWatch logging.
- Automatic ECS deployment rollback if the replacement task fails.

## 4. Public IP without public inbound access

The task runs in one of two public application subnets and receives an explicit public IPv4 address.

That address is needed for outbound connections because we deliberately avoid the recurring cost of a NAT gateway. The task uses its public address to contact services such as:

- OpenAI.
- Cognito’s public key endpoint.
- ECR during image startup.
- Secrets Manager.
- CloudWatch Logs.

A public IP does not automatically make the containers publicly reachable. The task’s security group accepts inbound traffic only from the ALB security group on port 8501.

There is no inbound rule for:

- Port 8000.
- SSH.
- Arbitrary internet traffic.

This is a cost-conscious learning architecture, not the usual production preference of private tasks behind a NAT gateway or VPC endpoints.

## 5. Authentication and authorization

The completed browser authentication journey will be:

1. Operator opens the CloudFront URL.
2. Streamlit redirects the browser to Cognito.
3. Cognito redirects the operator to Google.
4. Google authenticates the selected test user.
5. Google returns the result to Cognito.
6. Cognito returns an authorization code to the CloudFront application URL.
7. Streamlit exchanges the code for Cognito tokens.
8. Streamlit sends the Cognito access token to FastAPI.
9. FastAPI validates the token.
10. The application checks membership in the `operators` group.

FastAPI verifies:

- Cryptographic signature.
- Cognito issuer.
- Cognito app-client ID.
- Token expiry.
- That it is an access token.
- Subject identity.
- Cognito group claims.

Authentication and authorization remain separate:

- Cognito establishes who the user is.
- The application’s OperatorAuthorizer decides whether that identity may perform operator actions.

A valid Google/Cognito user without the operators group receives HTTP 403. A missing or invalid token receives HTTP 401.

The Terraform resources for Cognito are defined, but the Streamlit authorization-code session and Google federation are the next implementation work before starting the service.

## 6. Model inference and secrets

At task startup, ECS retrieves the OpenAI API key from Secrets Manager and injects it into the API container as OPENAI_API_KEY.

The credential is not:

- Committed to Git.
- Stored in a Terraform variable.
- Stored in Terraform state.
- Passed to the Streamlit container.
- Printed as a Terraform output.

When an authorized operator asks a question:

Browser
  -> CloudFront
  -> ALB
  -> Streamlit
  -> FastAPI
  -> OpenAI
  -> FastAPI
  -> Streamlit
  -> Browser

The existing application limits still apply: bounded input size, one active generation per process, bounded model turns and tool calls, deadlines, and disabled provider retries.

## 7. Immutable container delivery

ECR stores the application image.

The deployment references an exact digest:

123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/support-desk@sha256:...

A digest identifies the exact image contents. Unlike a mutable tag such as latest, it cannot silently point to a different image later.

Both containers use the same digest but start different commands:

- API container starts Uvicorn/FastAPI.
- UI container starts Streamlit.

ECR also:

- Prevents tag replacement.
- Scans images when pushed.
- Retains the ten newest images.
- Refuses automatic recursive deletion.

Keeping previous image digests enables an explicit rollback to a known application version.

## 8. Deployment and rollback behavior

When deploying a new digest, ECS creates a replacement task and checks its health.

If the new task becomes healthy:

old task -> drained and stopped
new task -> receives ALB traffic

If startup or health checks fail:

new task -> rejected
ECS circuit breaker -> restores previous task definition

The later delivery workflow will also record the previous task-definition revision so rollback can be demonstrated deliberately, rather than relying only on automatic failure recovery.

Because the desired count is one, deployments may have limited availability during replacement. This is acceptable for the bounded learning deployment but is not a high-availability production target.

## 9. Terraform state and GitHub access

Terraform state lives in the encrypted, versioned S3 bucket created by the bootstrap stack.

There are two independent state objects:

bootstrap/terraform.tfstate
learning/platform.tfstate

The first records the state bucket and GitHub roles. The second will record the application infrastructure.

GitHub Actions will authenticate to AWS using OIDC:

GitHub workflow
    |
    | short-lived signed OIDC token
    v
AWS IAM role

No long-lived AWS access key needs to be stored in GitHub.

Separate protected GitHub environments and roles distinguish:

- Infrastructure planning.
- Infrastructure application.

The roles currently have state-only permissions. The next delivery unit will add reviewed AWS permissions for planning and changing the specific platform resources.

## 10. Network layout

The VPC uses 10.32.0.0/16 and contains six subnets:

| Tier | Purpose | Internet route |
|---|---|---|
| Origin 1 and 2 | Internal ALB and CloudFront VPC origin | No |
| Application 1 and 2 | Fargate task with explicit public IP | Yes |
| Database 1 and 2 | Future private RDS PostgreSQL | No |

The two subnets in each tier are in different Availability Zones.

No NAT gateway is created. This is one of the largest cost-saving choices in the design.

## 11. What is not deployed yet

Applying the current Slice 1.3 Terraform will not create:

- An RDS database.
- Application persistence.
- Phoenix, Prometheus, or Grafana.
- A custom domain.
- A NAT gateway.
- High-availability application tasks.
- Google federation credentials.
- The OpenAI secret value.

The database subnets and subnet group merely reserve the correct private destination for RDS in a later slice.

## End-to-end mental model

The architecture separates responsibilities into layers:

| Layer | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| CloudFront | Public HTTPS and private entry into the VPC |
| Internal ALB | Health-check and route traffic to Streamlit |
| Streamlit | Operator browser interface and authenticated session |
| FastAPI | Authentication enforcement and application boundary |
| Cognito + Google | Operator identity |
| Application authorization | Enforce operators membership |
| ECS/Fargate | Run the UI and API containers |
| ECR | Store immutable application images |
| Secrets Manager | Supply the model credential at runtime |
| CloudWatch | Retain container logs |
| S3 | Store Terraform state |
| Terraform | Describe and reconcile the AWS infrastructure |
| GitHub OIDC | Give workflows temporary AWS credentials |
| Future RDS | Durable application records in later slices |

The central security boundary is: CloudFront is public, the ALB is private, only Streamlit is reachable through the ALB, FastAPI is task-local, and FastAPI still independently enforces authorization on every protected application request.
